executiveSummary: GM0505 passes the complete deterministic execution contract over all ten canonical scenarios, T+0/6/12/24/48/72 and all eight essential services. Its CBS/PDOK identity, 2025 generalized boundary, 122,796 residents, 132 neighbourhoods and Zuid-Holland-Zuid safety-region assignment reconcile. Release remains correction-required. The current model retains an N3 Dordrecht-Papendrecht logical edge while Rijkswaterstaat has the Papendrechtsebrug closed in both directions from 17 July 2026 through 21 April 2027, and that road edge is reused for every service. The river preset reports normalized inundation stress 2.4258, 71,631 affected people-equivalent at T+24 and 74,762 at T+72 without a selected dike-ring-22 breach/overtopping trajectory, LIWO footprint, tidal/river boundary conditions or recession. The coastal preset gives zero direct flood stress despite Dordrecht's official sea/storm-plus-river and tidal outer-dike pathways. Eight nonzero standalone hazards reuse exactly one complete neighbourhood order, and a controlled wildfire source inside the Dordtse Biesbosch neighbourhood ranks that containing neighbourhood 130th of 132. Public registers, provider areas, one current water level, grid-planning values and facility points are valuable typed context but do not validate physical topology, capacity, live state, backup, stock or restoration. Official evacuation, quay, flood-defence and 72-hour preparedness evidence should become optional, time-stamped actions and constraints rather than implied outcomes. The exact scenario numbers remain deterministic exercise outputs, not observations, warnings, forecasts or operator commitments.

evidenceSources.title: Kerncijfers wijken en buurten 2025 — filtered rows for GM0505
supports: Official-context GM0505/Dordrecht identity, population 122,796, density 1,583 residents per square kilometre, 20.2% aged 65 or older and 23,817 one-person households.

The machine-readable OData table is an annual CC BY 4.0 statistical release. Published neighbourhood counts are rounded and some values are suppressed, unavailable or not applicable; null and Unknown must never become zero.

CBS aggregates support population reconciliation and vulnerability context, not event-time visitors, medically dependent individuals, evacuation behaviour, household stocks or observed service demand.

evidenceSources.title: Gemeente and buurt gegeneraliseerd 2025 with BAG, BRT TOP10NL, NWB and railway context
evidenceSources.edition: CBS/BAG 2025; NWB 1 August 2026; BRT collection inspected 2 September 2026
supports: The application consumes CC BY 4.0 generalized CBS municipality/neighbourhood geometry. Generated centre [4.695671418452963, 51.787954663999116] lies inside GM0505; the separately versioned BAG Dordrecht label point lies outside this generalized polygon and is an edition/generalization caveat, not an identity failure.

BAG woonplaatsen are available through https://api.pdok.nl/kadaster/bag/ogc/v2/collections/woonplaats under Public Domain Mark 1.0. BRT TOP10NL at https://api.pdok.nl/kadaster/brt-top10nl/ogc/v1 is CC BY 4.0 with rotating updates and supplies seven settlement labels and source-scaled terrain context.

Monthly CC0 NWB geometry is downloadable at https://downloads.rijkswaterstaatdata.nl/nwb-wegen/geogegevens/shapefile/NWB-light/01-08-2026.zip. The generated graph has A16 links toward Moerdijk and Zwijndrecht, N3 toward Papendrecht and N217 toward Hoeksche Waard; scenario units are not measured traffic capacity.

ProRail OGC https://api.pdok.nl/prorail/spoorwegen/ogc/v1 is CC0 static infrastructure context with manual cadence; three stations are assigned. The national GTFS feed is best-effort schedule context with no operational-service guarantee. Geometry and timetables do not establish incident passability.

evidenceSources.title: Hoogwater in Dordrecht, Dordtse Omgevingsvisie 2.0 and Water- en Rioleringsprogramma 2026–2030
evidenceSources.edition: Current high-water guidance inspected 2 September 2026; Omgevingsvisie adopted 23 September 2025; WRP 2026–2030
supports: The current page says tidal high-water peaks last a few hours, occur twice per 24 hours and can recur over one or more days. It identifies low outer-dike streets/quays and polder/nature areas, and notes groundwater can recede later than the river.

A forecast of +1.80 m NAP triggers the municipal mail warning; at +2.10 m NAP or more the municipality closes threatened quays and offers sandbags, with possible parking bans, a sound truck, current information and island-water-system management. These are conditional triggers, not a forecast or proof of completion.

The adopted Omgevingsvisie 2.0 is at https://raad.dordrecht.nl/Vergaderingen/Gemeenteraad-Dordrecht-1/2025/23-september/14%3A00/Vaststellen-Dordtse-Omgevingsvisie-2-0-Eiland-met-kwaliteit-Raadsvoorstel/30-1-Dordtse-Omgevingsvisie-2-0-Eiland-met-kwaliteit-Geamendeerd-Vastgesteld.pdf. It treats both river and sea/storm flooding, states roughly 15% can evacuate horizontally in about 48 hours and relies on safe places on the island for others; this is planning context, not observed behaviour or refuge availability.

The municipal WRP is downloadable at https://raad.dordrecht.nl/Documenten/Wrp-Dordrecht-2026-2030-def-0310-PvE-1.pdf and distinguishes wastewater, rainwater, groundwater and surface water. The documents have no blanket machine-data licence or fixed update cadence; underlying municipal GIS needs an authorized, versioned export.

evidenceSources.title: Regionaal Risicoprofiel Zuid-Holland Zuid 2025–2028, Regionaal Crisisplan 2026–2029 and 72-hour guidance
evidenceSources.edition: Risk profile adopted 5 December 2024; crisis plan 2026–2029; guidance inspected 2 September 2026
supports: The profile identifies dike ring 22 Eiland van Dordrecht, managed by Waterschap Hollandse Delta, and river, sea/storm and combined flooding. It also covers extreme rain, heat/drought, snow/ice, storm, long power/digital disruption and drinking-water disruption.

It describes electricity, gas, drinking water, voice/data, bridges, tunnels and data centres as interdependent and identifies Evides as Dordrecht's drinking-water supplier. Official risk description is not an outage probability, physical network or restoration curve.

Dordrecht has Seveso establishments and important hazardous-goods road, rail, river and port transport. Large contiguous forest/heath/dune areas over 100 ha are not a dominant regional nature-fire feature; Hollandsche Biesbosch visitors remain locally relevant. Strong damaging earthquake is not a characteristic local scenario, while Doel and Borssele remain radiological planning context outside the municipality.

The current crisis plan is available at https://www.zhzveilig.nl/sites/zhzveilig_corporate/files/2026-01/regionaal_crisisplan_2026-2029_veiligheidsregio_zuid-holland_zuid.pdf and defines CoPI/ROT, GHOR, police, fire and population-care roles and assembly targets; roles and effort targets are not outcome guarantees. The 72-hour guidance at https://www.zhzveilig.nl/wat-doe-je-bij/weerbaarheid/denk-vooruit-boekje is preparedness advice, not measured household stock. No blanket reuse licence for the PDFs was established.

evidenceSources.publisher: Waterschap Hollandse Delta / Het Waterschapshuis / PDOK

evidenceSources.edition: Live OGC API inspected 2 September 2026; WSHD surface-water register 2023 under revision

Contributor coverage is partial; point/register status is not live operational state, topology, capacity, direction, setpoint, backup or restoration.

Waterketen DAMO is available at https://api.pdok.nl/hwh/waterschappen-waterketen-damo/ogc/v1 and Waterbeheergebieden IMWA at https://api.pdok.nl/hwh/waterschappen-waterbeheergebieden-imwa/ogc/v1 under CC BY-SA 4.0; contributor cadence and completeness vary.

The WSHD surface-water register page https://www.wshd.nl/legger-oppervlaktewaterlichamen-kunstwerken-0 describes legal ditches, pumps, weirs and maintenance obligations and warns the 2023 register is being updated. Regional-defence maps/downloads are at https://www.wshd.nl/legger-regionale-waterkeringen and use AHN4 profiles.

WSHD's Dordrecht storm/high-water practice includes the Voorstraat primary defence, boards/coupures and exercises. Register geometry and exercises provide context; neither proves event-time closure, pump operation, defence performance or service continuity.

evidenceSources.publisher: Provincie Zuid-Holland / WMCN Rijkswaterstaat / IPLO / KNMI
evidenceSources.title: Authoritative extreme-rain, flood-scenario, water-level and weather/seismic integration routes
evidenceSources.edition: PZH 100 mm/2 h scenario circa 2018, catalogue updated 19 August 2026; LIWO release 2025.1.6; live feeds inspected 2 September 2026
supports: The province publishes a 100 mm in two hours static urban-extreme-rain depth scenario, modelled with 3Di/AHN/land/soil and approximately 0.25 square metre source cells, as Public Domain WMS https://geodata.zuid-holland.nl/geoserver/klimaat/wms?service=WMS&version=1.3.0&request=GetCapabilities and GeoTIFF Atom download https://geo.zuid-holland.nl/Data/atom/waterdiepte_bij_extreme_neerslag_stedelijk.xml. Municipal submodels may include sewer effects; model-information and NoData layers must be retained.

LIWO is documented at https://iplo.nl/thema/water/applicaties-modellen/berichtgeving-crisismanagement/liwo/ and available via https://basisinformatie-overstromingen.nl/geoserver/ows. Release 2025.1.6 is an irregular expert-use scenario library, not a forecast; each integration must retain selected breach/overtopping/defence case, river/sea/tide boundary, probability class, depth, arrival, duration/recession, resolution, licence and NoData.

RWS Waterinfo supplies observations, forecasts and expectations with distinct valid times. The deployed assignment has one Dordrecht Oude Maas/Beneden Merwede level: 72 cm NAP observed 2 September 2026 17:30Z and retrieved 18:03Z. It is a current point observation, not surface coverage or a T+72 scenario. Waterinfo is commonly ten-minute and CC0 unless a component states otherwise.

KNMI radar WMS supplies five-minute observed precipitation and KNMI EDR https://developer.dataplatform.knmi.nl/edr-api versioned observations/forecasts under dataset-specific terms, commonly CC BY 4.0. KNMI FDSN https://rdsa.knmi.nl/fdsnws/event/1/ is event-point context and cannot replace selected ShakeMap/ground-motion/site-response data.

evidenceSources.title: Papendrechtsebrug renovation and valid-time road/crossing context
evidenceSources.edition: Current project state inspected 2 September 2026; NDW snapshot publication 2 September 2026 15:25Z
supports: Rijkswaterstaat states the N3 Papendrechtsebrug is closed to all road traffic in both directions from 17 July 2026 through 21 April 2027, with 30–60 minutes extra travel time. The Baanhoekbrug path is temporarily reserved for emergency services and two ferries serve cyclists/pedestrians. Planning can change, so valid time and retrieval time are mandatory.

The official Drechttunnel page https://www.rijkswaterstaat.nl/wegen/wegenoverzicht/a16/drechttunnel-a16 identifies the A16 crossing between Dordrecht and Zwijndrecht. https://kiltunnel.nl/home identifies the N217 Kiltunnel connection between Dordrecht Island and Hoeksche Waard. Static municipal edges do not encode bridge/tunnel state, direction, mode, dangerous-goods restrictions or throughput.

NDW situation data is CC0 unless stated otherwise and useful only with publication/start/end/last-update semantics. The deployed snapshot intersects one broken-down-vehicle record but does not causally close the N3 edge; no NDW record never means all roads are open and a current snapshot must not be projected silently to T+72.

A16 Dordrecht-Moerdijk and Dordrecht-Zwijndrecht graph edges share one physical corridor identity on opposite sides and are not independent additive measured capacity. Waterway, ferry and rail alternatives are absent from the municipal transfer graph.

evidenceSources.publisher: Evides / Stedin / Netbeheer Nederland / RIVM / RDI / DUO / KVK
evidenceSources.title: Public service territories, planning-capacity and critical-facility/register context for Dordrecht
evidenceSources.edition: Provider/register snapshots retrieved in 2026; RIVM acute-care v1.1 published 3 July 2026
supports: Evides says Baanhoek supplies Dordrecht and eastern Hoeksche Waard using Brabantse Biesbosch surface water plus deep groundwater from Eiland van Dordrecht. Its July 2026 preparedness account at https://www.zhzveilig.nl/wat-doe-je-bij/stroomuitval/partnerverhaal-0 states operator-level emergency power/diesel preparedness but notes building pumps above the fourth floor can fail during blackout. This is operator guidance, not a municipal availability guarantee.

Public provider WMS at the sampled municipal centre identifies Stedin electricity (timestamp 24 March 2026), Stedin gas (17 December 2025), Evides water (12 May 2026) and Ziggo media (7 September 2025). Provider-area polygons are Public Domain or publisher-specified context; a centre-point query is not full coverage, topology, capacity or state.

Netbeheer Nederland's machine planning context for sampled postcode 3319SC reports Dordrecht Centrum en Oost withdrawal existing/required/queue 36.7/85.5/1.6 MW and seven queued requests, with five projects earliest 2027. Capacity/project data are generally quarterly and queue data monthly; the exact reuse licence was not established. One large-user planning polygon cannot drive household outage or restoration.

RIVM's CC0 acute-care dataset identifies Albert Schweitzer Ziekenhuis with 24/7 emergency and acute-obstetric functions, 24 treatment rooms and 31,736 visits in 2025; these are role/capacity context, not live occupancy, staffing, generator fuel or access. RDI returns 195 antenna-site records, DUO 91 location-use records and KVK 23 government-address records in GM0505. Their machine feeds have differing cadence/licence; locations do not establish coverage/backhaul, shelter, reception, supply, roles or operational state.

notes: BAG assigns one woonplaats, Dordrecht. Its label point [4.752523197196705, 51.7687409147717] is outside the independently generalized 2025 CBS polygon; this is retained as a boundary/version caveat rather than deleting or reassigning the place.
BRT labels Bovenhoek, De Griend, Dordrecht, Kop van 't Land, Tweede Tol, Wieldrecht and Willemsdorp as three buurtschappen, three deelkernen and one woonkern.

transport.summary: The four-edge graph omits crossing state and currently contradicts the official N3 Papendrechtsebrug closure.
notes: Generated edges are A16 to Moerdijk at 260 scenario units, A16 to Zwijndrecht at 260, N3 to Papendrecht at 150 and N217 to Hoeksche Waard at 150. These are logical bounds, not measured lane/evacuation throughput.

At audit time the N3 bridge is officially closed in both directions, but the current graph retains the link and supplies no valid-time closure. All services can use it because supportedServices is absent.

Drechttunnel, Moerdijk bridge, Papendrechtsebrug and Kiltunnel are not represented as stateful assets. Three ProRail stations and 185 GTFS stop areas are static infrastructure/schedule context; rail, waterway and temporary ferry capacity/state are absent.
One deployed NDW incident is not a complete road-state graph. Absence of a live record cannot mean open, and the current snapshot cannot be advanced to T+72.

emergencyContext.summary: Official warning, evacuation, defence, crisis-role and 72-hour guidance exists, but no event-time action/resource/completion state is modelled.
notes: Dordrecht has conditional +1.80/+2.10 m NAP municipal actions, an island evacuation/refuge concept, dike and Voorstraat-defence responsibilities, and safety-region CoPI/ROT/GHOR/population-care roles. None is automatically triggered by a normalized model index.

Planning says only roughly 15% can leave horizontally within about 48 hours and others need safe places on the island. The simulator neither moves population nor records accessible, opened and stocked refuge/reception locations.

Preparedness guidance and operator statements do not measure household water/food/medication, facility fuel, staff, beds, distribution stocks, pump state, vehicles, crews or restoration. Those states remain Unknown until event-authorized.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten presets produce complete finite deterministic output at all six checkpoints and all eight services; calibration and semantics failures are recorded separately.
notes: The focused gate executed severe storm, pluvial flood, river flood, coastal flood, heatwave, winter storm, cyberattack, earthquake, wildfire and compound at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 for power, water, drainage, gas, telecom, mobility, facilities and supply.

At T+24 severity / post-network pressure / affected people-equivalent / cumulative local pre-network event-attributable person-hours are storm 0.2311 / 0.2825 / 24,659 / 743,041.44; pluvial 0.5093 / 0.3273 / 32,403 / 657,956.30; river 0.7633 / 0.5540 / 71,631 / 1,123,155.33; coastal 0.0294 / 0.2413 / 17,520 / 67,940.41; heat 0.1136 / 0.2020 / 10,719 / 346,347.97.

At T+72 river severity and stress remain 0.7633/2.4258, pressure 0.5721, affected 74,762 and person-hours 4,313,902.42; compound remains severity 0.6715, pressure 0.6282 and affected 84,467. These are exercise outputs, not observations, probabilities, warnings or restoration forecasts.

numericalInvariants.summary: The focused gate passes deterministic, finite, zero-intensity, causal, allocation, reconciliation and monotonic-burden contracts.
notes: MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM0505 pnpm audit:model passed both tests on current code across 10 presets × 6 checkpoints × 8 services.

Every intensity-zero run has exactly zero event severity, affected people-equivalent and event-attributable deprived person-hours at every checkpoint; repeated output and scenario/web preset parity pass.
All 132 local rows allocate exactly 122,796 residents. Maximum population, demand and delivery reconciliation error is 1.4210854715202004e-13.
Changing selected service produces maximum local-hazard delta zero; cumulative event-attributable person-hours are monotonic and declared logical-route bounds hold.

spatialPlausibility.summary: One shared neighbourhood order and a failed local-fire source ranking cannot represent Dordrecht's mechanism-specific geography.
notes: At T+24 all eight nonzero standalone presets have the exact same complete 132-neighbourhood order, led by Vogelplein-Aalscholverstraat, Zeehavenlaan, Dordtse Kil III, Heysterbachstraat, Amstelwijck-West, Spaarbekken, Krabbepolder and Dordtse Kil I. Earthquake is an all-zero local tie; compound differs through saturation.
That equality cannot represent separate outer-dike/tidal, dike-ring, rainfall/terrain/sewer, heat/vulnerability, winter/wind, cyber-target and smoke/fire mechanisms.

A controlled synthetic wildfire point [4.6869211427584085, 51.75286293610363] lies inside BU05059804 Dordtse Biesbosch and inside a BRT TOP10NL broadleaf-forest polygon, yet that containing neighbourhood ranks 130/132 at local hazard 0.3418 while unrelated neighbourhoods lead near 0.48. BRT's feature source actuality is 2014, so it is aged land-cover context rather than current fuel/moisture evidence.

serviceDependencies.summary: All eight service balances are inspectable, but one four-road logical graph cannot represent Dordrecht's physical lifelines or exact 72-hour availability.
notes: Every GM0505 route omits supportedServices, so power, water, drainage, gas, telecom, mobility, facilities and supply all reuse A16/N3/N217 road edges; the currently closed N3 edge can therefore affect every service.

At river T+24 modeled availability is power 0.4451, water 0.4348, drainage 0.2604, gas 0.6953, telecom 0.4683, mobility 0.3910, facilities 0.5024 and supply 0.3647. No cited operator or authority validates those exact percentages, dependencies or repair paths.

The water inspector shows 89 scenario units/hour demand, 39 delivered, 7.3-hour reserve and reductions of 31.9 percentage points direct inundation, 15.4 power dependency, 6.45 baseline and 2.76 network transfer, with no restoration. Those transparent arithmetic components remain uncalibrated proxies.

Provider, NBNL, HWH, RDI, care, school and government-register geometry is non-causal context. It does not establish feeder/pipe/sewer/backhaul topology, pressure/quality, load, control, priority, backup, stock, crew or restoration.

causalTrace.summary: Stage arithmetic and local pre-network versus post-network scope are disclosed, but evidence class, valid time and physical semantics still require persistent machine-readable labels.
notes: The model quarter-hour-integrates event-attributable local pre-network service shortfall against a matched no-event baseline, then computes current system pressure and affected people-equivalent after service-network transfer. These are intentionally different scopes and are not observed customers.

Browser inspection at 1440×900 and 390×844 for GM0505 river/water at T+24 and T+72 showed the inspector's official-context/scenario labels, logical-transfer caveat and a live T+24 announcement: 'Drinking water. Dordrecht: critical, 43% available.' No console errors or horizontal overflow occurred.

Current Waterinfo/NDW/provider snapshots, static registers/planning scenarios, adopted plans and the synthetic T+72 trajectory remain different evidence and time classes. An observation or empty response must not silently initialize or validate a future scenario.
Hazard, baseline, dependency, backup, intervention, transfer and reconciliation arithmetic closes, but causal auditability does not make unsupported topology or calibration physical.

recovery72h.summary: Persistent river/compound curves and other recovery paths are deterministic but not calibrated to Dordrecht hydrology, crossings, operators, facilities, supplies or action completion.
notes: River direct severity/stress reaches 0.7633/2.4258 at T+12 and remains identical through T+72; seven services plateau from T+48 to T+72, while facilities declines further. No selected hydrograph, tidal phase, defence state, inundation arrival/recession or operator restoration plan supports the plateau.

Pluvial rain peaks earlier, direct stress clears by T+48, while heat keeps 26.17 C and drought 0.6314 through T+72. These generic curves are not tied to a versioned PZH rain raster, KNMI issue/valid time, local urban heat exposure or measured drainage/restoration.

Compound T+48 and T+72 availability is an exact plateau for seven services, with facilities changing from its earlier state; at T+72 availability is power 0.3666, water 0.3634, drainage 0.2684, gas 0.5786, telecom 0.2459, mobility 0.4959, facilities 0.3414 and supply 0.3408. Persistent impact can be a conservative exercise, but these values are unvalidated.

No current bridge/tunnel graph, utility switching, water quality/pressure, sewer/control telemetry, crew/fuel/spares, hospital acceptance, temporary water/reception point, household stock, evacuation/refuge movement or action-completion evidence is ingested. Seventy-two hours is a planning horizon, not a recovery deadline.

findings.summary: The current graph keeps a nominal N3 Dordrecht-Papendrecht edge while the Papendrechtsebrug is officially closed in both directions.
findings.evidence: E07 states the N3 bridge is closed to all road traffic from 17 July 2026 through 21 April 2027, with 30–60 minutes extra travel time, temporary emergency use of the Baanhoek path and two cyclist/pedestrian ferries. The generated GM0505 graph still includes N3 to GM0590 at 150 nominal scenario units, without valid time, crossing asset or supportedServices; all eight services may use it. The deployed 2 September NDW snapshot has one unrelated broken-down-vehicle record and does not causally apply the planned closure. NWB geometry and absent live incidents do not establish passability.
findings.action: Add scenario/reference valid time and a crossing-state layer. In a current-state mode spanning the official interval, close or mark Unknown the N3 road edge and represent Baanhoek emergency access and ferries as separate mode-limited, time-bounded alternatives with capacity Unknown. Never project an NDW snapshot to T+72 or map a road edge onto physical utilities; regression-test both open and closed valid-time cases.

findings.summary: The river preset produces a very large persistent Dordrecht impact without a selected dike-ring-22 flood scenario or hydrodynamic provenance.
findings.evidence: River forcing rises from zero at T+0 to severity/stress 0.2687/0.8539 at T+6 and 0.7633/2.4258 at T+12, then remains 0.7633/2.4258 through T+72. Post-network pressure/affected people-equivalent is T+6 0.3531/36,860, T+12 0.5141/64,721, T+24 0.5540/71,631, T+48 and T+72 0.5721/74,762. E03–E06 establish dike ring 22, outer-dike tidal peaks, river/sea/combined mechanisms, defences and multiple official scenario libraries, but the output has no selected breach or overtopping, defence state, Rhine/Meuse discharge, sea/tide boundary, depth units, footprint, arrival, duration/recession, probability class or NoData. A stress value above one is a model index, not observed metres or probability.
findings.action: Label the current magnitude and neighbourhood layer unsupported/diagnostic, not forecast or official flood map. Require an authority-selected, versioned LIWO/WSHD/RWS exercise case with scenario ID, defence/breach/overtopping assumptions, water boundary/hydrograph and datum, tide/storm combination, depth/velocity/arrival/recession, probability class, resolution, licence, coverage and NoData before local impact claims. Keep current Waterinfo observations separate.

findings.summary: Zero direct coastal-flood stress is too narrow for Dordrecht unless the UI explicitly excludes sea/storm-driven tidal and combined pathways.
findings.evidence: At coastal T+24 the model reports direct flood stress exactly zero, overall severity 0.0294, wind 17.45 m/s, pressure 0.2413 and 17,520 affected people-equivalent; direct forcing clears by T+72 while residual pressure is 0.1107. E03 says Dordrecht has tidal peaks and low outer-dike quays/polder/nature areas. E04 treats Eiland van Dordrecht flooding from river, sea/storm and their combination. Zero for one unselected synthetic coastal mechanism cannot mean no storm-surge, tide, outer-dike, groundwater or combined exposure.
findings.action: Give the coastal preset a precise inclusion/exclusion statement and show local water exposure as Unknown until a selected sea/tide/river/defence scenario is bound. Keep wind as a separate forcing component. If direct water is modelled, use the same versioned LIWO/RWS/WSHD scenario contract as river flooding and test that zero never renders as an all-clear for excluded pathways.

findings.summary: Eight unrelated nonzero standalone hazards reuse exactly one complete 132-neighbourhood ranking.
findings.evidence: At T+24 severe storm, pluvial flood, river flood, coastal flood, heatwave, winter storm, cyberattack and canonical wildfire rank all 132 neighbourhoods identically, led by Vogelplein-Aalscholverstraat, Zeehavenlaan, Dordtse Kil III, Heysterbachstraat, Amstelwijck-West, Spaarbekken, Krabbepolder and Dordtse Kil I. The equality conflicts with official distinctions among outer-dike quays, dike-ring scenarios, pluvial depths, urban heat/vulnerability, wind, industrial/ICT targets and vegetation. Zero-resident Krabbepolder may legitimately carry business/system demand, but its rank still requires hazard-specific evidence.
findings.action: Mark the eight GM0505 neighbourhood hazard layers unsupported until mechanism-specific, coverage-aware inputs replace the common seed. Prefer selected LIWO/WSHD flood surfaces, PZH 100 mm/2 h depth and model-information rasters, KNMI valid-time wind/temperature/radar, selected cyber target sets and source/perimeter-based fire. Preserve CRS, units, edition/valid time, resolution, licence, coverage and NoData and assert unrelated hazards no longer have identical complete ranks.

findings.summary: A controlled wildfire source inside Dordtse Biesbosch fails source-containment spatial plausibility by ranking its containing neighbourhood 130th of 132.
findings.evidence: The controlled source [4.6869211427584085, 51.75286293610363] is inside official BU05059804 Dordtse Biesbosch and an intersecting BRT TOP10NL terrain_vlak classified broadleaf forest. findings.action: Make source containment/distance a release invariant for configured local fire. findings.summary: Storm, pluvial, heat/drought, winter, cyber, earthquake and canonical wildfire remain generic scenario families rather than locally calibrated Dordrecht forecasts.

findings.summary: Dordrecht's Seveso, port, dangerous-goods transport and radiological-planning risks are outside the ten-preset scope.

findings.action: Disclose these hazards as out of scope. residualLimitations: This is a deterministic first-72-hour planning-model audit, not a KNMI, Rijkswaterstaat, WMCN, Waterschap Hollandse Delta, Veiligheidsregio Zuid-Holland-Zuid, municipality, province or infrastructure-operator forecast, warning, probability, evacuation order, casualty estimate or restoration commitment.

The 2025 generalized CBS boundary and neighbourhoods are suitable for overview aggregation, not parcel hydraulics, dike compartments, outer-dike exposure, water/land separation, asset ownership, incident perimeters or emergency routes.

No selected dike-ring-22 breach/overtopping/defence case, Rhine/Meuse discharge, sea/tide boundary, water-level datum, connected flood footprint, depth/velocity, arrival/recession, probability class or NoData mask drives GM0505.

The PZH 100 mm/2 h product is a static official planning scenario, not observed rain or a T+72 forecast; municipal submodel/sewer inclusion varies and its model-information/NoData layer must remain attached.
HWH/WSHD water objects are legal/register geometry without guaranteed live completeness, topology, capacity, flow direction, setpoint, condition, operation, backup or restoration.

Current Waterinfo, NDW, provider and other snapshots have distinct observation/retrieval/valid times. Missing records mean Unknown, not zero hazard, open road, functioning service or a valid future state.

NWB, ProRail and GTFS are static geometry/schedule context. They do not establish crossing state, incident-time passability, evacuation throughput, rail/waterway/ferry alternatives or T+72 continuity.

No complete safe public source supplies Stedin feeder/gas topology, Evides distribution pressure/quality topology, municipal sewer connectivity, water-board live controls, telecom backhaul, facility dependencies, stocks, backups, crews or restoration. Sensitive details were not inferred.

All eight services currently reuse four road-derived logical links. Those links cannot be interpreted as physical electricity, gas, potable-water, wastewater, surface-water-control, telecom, patient-transfer or stocked-logistics networks.

RIVM acute-care role and annual volume do not establish live occupancy, staffing, acceptance/diversion, generator fuel, backup endurance or route access. RDI sites do not establish radio coverage, traffic, power/backhaul, availability or restoration; DUO/KVK addresses do not establish reception, shelter or distribution roles.

The controlled wildfire point is synthetic and tests source containment only; BRT source actuality is aged and no current fuel/moisture, wind, perimeter, suppression-water, access, evacuation or smoke-exposure model is calibrated.

Cyber lacks a named target, architecture and attack path; earthquake lacks a selected local event and ground-motion/site-response grid; industrial, port, dangerous-goods, radiological, pandemic and major urban-fire events are outside the ten presets.

Household preparedness, medically dependent residents, visitors/workers, mutual aid, reception/refuge/water points, medicine, food/fuel, staff, vehicles and repair priorities remain assumptions or Unknown. Official 72-hour guidance is not measured readiness or an aid/recovery deadline.

Affected population is a current post-network people-equivalent threshold metric, while deprived person-hours is a cumulative local pre-network matched-baseline service-pressure proxy. Neither is identified customers, casualties, displacement, welfare loss or economic damage; six-hour checkpoints can miss tidal and fast pluvial changes.
